Stacy — thanks for the quick note. High level answers up front, then a short example calc and proposed smoothing/POC language below. I've attached a concise commercial appendix for your finance team.

High level:
- Billable units: generation tokens (prompt + generated tokens) billed per 1k gen-tokens; embeddings billed per 1k embedding vectors (we normalize vector calls to a 1k-vector unit). Chat messages that re-use cached prefix tokens only bill new generated tokens.
- Smoothing: we offer a 3-month smoothing window for committed customers (rolling average). Smoothing reduces the impact of short spikes; missed commit usage below a 90% threshold triggers a grace band before true-up.
- POC commit: we support short-term POC commits (30–90 days) with an introductory price floor and pre-agreed burst cushion. POC terms can convert to a longer reserved commit with crediting applied to the first invoice after conversion.

Quick pricing table (examples; final pricing is subscription/region dependent):
- On-demand (hosted): $0.0012 / gen-k-token; $0.00075 / embedding-k-vector
- 12-month reserved commit (tier 1): 5M gen-k-tokens/month at $0.0009 / gen-k-token (10% comp action discount for first year)
- Overage tiers: 0–10% above commit = billed at commitment rate + 15% premium; 10–50% = commitment rate + 40% premium; >50% = on-demand rate

Example (monthly):
- Commit: 5M gen-k-tokens at $0.0009 = $4,500/month
- Month spike: 6M gen-k-tokens used (20% over commit) -> first 10% (500k) billed at $0.0009 * 1.15, next 10% (500k) billed at $0.0009 * 1.40

Smoothing / True-up proposal (recommended for Orion):
- Rolling 3-month smoothing: monthly invoices indicate raw usage; chargeable usage is the 3-month rolling average (month t-2, t-1, t).
- Grace band: if rolling average < 90% of committed level and no pattern of sustained underutilization, no immediate penalty; finance applies a one-time advisory true-up at contract anniversary.
- Annual true-up: net positive or negative true-ups reconcile at the annual billing date; credits apply to the following month.

Thanks — will stand by for questions.

Stacy — adding a few concrete guardrails you can share with finance/legal. We keep the language intentionally simple so the procurement team can map to Orion's TCO model.

1) Unit definitions
- Gen-token unit: billed per 1k generated tokens (includes prompt tokens + model output tokens). For stream/cached sessions we charge only incremental new tokens.
- Embedding unit: billed per 1k embeddings (we count an embedding API call as 1 vector; large-batch normalization provided in appendix).

2) Commit & price ladder
- Example commit tiers (monthly equivalent): 1M / 5M / 20M gen-k-tokens
- Pricing: 1M @ $0.00105, 5M @ $0.0009, 20M @ $0.00068 (discount scale applies with longer terms and higher $commit).

3) Smoothing, grace, and true-up mechanics
- Smoothing window: rolling 3-month average.
- Grace band: first 10% monthly variance forgiven on chargeback (applies automatically).
- True-up cadence: annual reconciliation; underutilization credits issued as account credit on the first invoice after true-up.

4) POC commit option
- Typical POC: 90-day commit equivalent to 10–20% of a forecasted 12-month commit. Special pricing floor: 15% below the 12-month committed rate for the pilot period. If customer converts to a 12-month commit within 60 days after POC, paid POC consumption is credited pro-rata to the new commit.

5) Overage treatment & capping
- Overage tiers as Alex outlined. We can also add a soft cap with e-mail triggers and optional auto-burst approvals.

6) SLA/crediting for latency targets (optional add-on)
- If we commit to a p99 latency SLA for a reserved pool and miss SLA > 2% of measurement windows, we apply credits as % of monthly invoice (formula in appendix).

Please see the attached spreadsheet for the sample TCO calc (tab "Orion Example"). If you want, we can produce a second tab showing a 6-month smoothing variant for comparison.

James — good questions. Quick responses below and a worked 3-month rolling example included. We can do invoice-level adjustments (legal-friendly) for true-up credits; they will be documented on the reconciliation invoice.

POC price & min guarantee: Redwood can offer a 60-day POC at $0.0008 / gen-k-token with a 250k gen-k-token minimum guarantee. Terms:
- Payment: invoice at POC completion for actual usage or the guaranteed minimum, whichever is higher.
- Credits: if customer converts to a 12-month commit within 45 days of POC completion, we credit any POC payments pro-rata to the first 3 months of the annual invoice (applied as invoice-level credit).

Worked example (simplified):
Assumptions: commit = 5M gen-k / month at $0.0009; smoothing = rolling 3-month average; months M1/M2/M3 usage = 4.2M / 6.0M / 5.4M gen-k
Raw monthly invoices (no smoothing):
- M1: 4.2M * $0.0009 = $3,780
- M2: 6.0M -> first 10% over = 500k @ (0.0009*1.15) = $517.5; next 400k @ (0.0009*1.40) = $504 -> base commit fulfilled otherwise; approximate M2 total = $5,940 (includes overage premiums)
- M3: 5.4M -> 400k over -> tiered premium; approx M3 total = $5,220
Rolling 3-month chargeable usage (avg):
- Chargeable M3 invoice uses avg(M1,M2,M3) = (4.2 + 6.0 + 5.4)/3 = 5.2M gen-k
- Chargeable amount at committed price: 5.2M * $0.0009 = $4,680 (invoice shows raw usage alongside the smoothed chargeable usage and overage breakdown)

Note: the invoice itself shows both raw monthly usage and the applied smoothing calculation line; any difference is reconciled at annual true-up and documented as an invoice-level credit if owed to the customer.
